text:
Rae Coleman: Dropping a new handoff mock for compact Autoscale row + surge tokens. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/hand-off/surge-tokens-compact. Problem we're solving: make it obvious where short-term capacity comes from and give a reversible path if guardrails are hit.
Omar Aziz: Nice. Two quick asks: 1) show which pool supplies surge tokens (icon + pool chip), 2) add an "undo" affordance after an apply that forced past guardrail. Users panic when they accidentally force. :grimacing:
Nina Park: For copy: prefer "Surge tokens (short)" over "Burst" in compact rows. Tooltip: "Surge tokens borrow spare GPUs for up to X minutes; may increase cost." Keep a 1-line mobile version.
Theo Silva: Accessibility: the surge token badge must include text and not just color. Use a lock icon when unavailable and `aria-disabled="true"`. Also add an offscreen summary for the whole row: `Autoscale min 1 max 8. Surge tokens: provided by Pool-B. SLO safe range: 20050ms.`
Rae Coleman: UX idea: when a user drags SLO slider outside guardrail, show an inline reversible action: `Force apply anyway (undo available for 5 minutes)` with `aria-live="polite"` announcing the change. Also show a collapsed timeline pill: `Applied 2m ago · undo` so they can revert.
Omar Aziz: Good. Implementation note: undo should revert both config and trigger a quick synthetic estimate to show new p95. UI should display the estimate delta and a tiny spinner while computing. Keep spinner accessible: `role=status` + offscreen text.
Nina Park: Edge case: hybrid configs (pinned + elastic pools). UI should make it explicit which pool is dominant for surge. Maybe show chips: `Pinned: pool-a` and `Surge: pool-b (3 tokens available)`. Clicking `Surge` chip opens pool picker pre-filtered to surge-capable pools.
Theo Silva: Keyboard flow: tab -> min input -> max input -> surge chip -> surge cap slider -> SLO slider -> info button -> apply. If a guardrail banner appears, focus moves into it. Escape returns to prior control. Banner has `role=alertdialog` with `aria-modal=false` so it's announced but not trapping.
Rae Coleman: Copy for guardrail banner: `Guardrail warning: this change may raise P95 above your target. Suggest: 450ms (safe).` Actions: `[Apply safe] [Force apply] [Learn more]`. `Learn more` opens a small inline explainer with the calculations used (window length, request distribution).
Omar Aziz: Tiny visual nit: when showing the delta chip near the slider use a neutral background and a thin border so it reads in both themes. Also make the delta `+N% cost · +Xm` compact.
Nina Park: A11y nit: when the delta updates because of traffic the `aria-live` should be debounced 300ms and we should avoid repeating unchanged messages. Also ensure scrubbing the slider doesn't flood AT.
Theo Silva: Localization: short labels like `Surge cap` should be translatable and avoid abbreviations. In some locales +/- signs appear after numbers, so keep the order flexible (`{cost} · {p95}`).
ux-helper-bot: Mock uploaded and pinned: https://www.figma.com/file/hand-off/surge-tokens-compact?node-id=5:12. @Rae Coleman added code snippets for the offscreen aria elements.
Rae Coleman: I'll update the mock with the timeline undo pill, the pool chips, and the offscreen summaries + aria ids. Tagging @Nina for accessibility review and @Omar for the apply/undo copy. Target: EOD tomorrow. :rocket:
